words.prose: {{ar:حمٓ}} ({{tr:ḥā mīm}}) fills the whole ayah while standing outside ordinary sentence grammar: it has no governor, case ending, predicate, subject, object, verbal event, or syntactic role to translate into a clause. The reader meets named letters before the Arabic sentence grid begins, and the verse closes before any internal predication can organize them. Its force is therefore threshold force, not lexical paraphrase. The opener remains both letter-names and performed sound: {{ar:ح}} ({{tr:ḥāʾ}}) and {{ar:م}} ({{tr:mīm}}) are heard as named alphabetic units, yet they also function as raw phonetic material at the doorway of discourse. Opacity is part of the meaning here; the letters are recognizable and pronounceable while their final semantic value is not reduced to one gloss. The no-root status blocks derivational decoding, so similarly shaped root families should not be imported. Classical readings may still create controlled secondary pressure: the abbreviation reading can let the surface hint at {{ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰن}} ({{tr:al-Raḥmān}}) without spelling the name out, and the ḥumma al-amr reading can let the sense "the matter has been decreed" hover behind the letters without replacing their local identity as disconnected letters. Form and performance also matter. The rasm binds two recited letter-names into one visible token, and the madd-marked surface cues duration rather than ordinary lexical segmentation. Waqf delivery may make the ayah land as two stopped beats, {{ar:ح}} ({{tr:ḥāʾ}}) then {{ar:م}} ({{tr:mīm}}), but that pause is acoustic texture, not a new word division or syntactic parse. The opener can also carry oath-like pressure without becoming a formal qasam construction, since the surface lacks the ordinary oath particles and case-marked sworn object. Across the mushaf, 46:1 is the closing node of the consecutive {{ar:حمٓ}} ({{tr:ḥā mīm}}) series at 40:1, 41:1, 42:1, 43:1, 44:1, 45:1, and 46:1, so this short ayah sounds like the final entry in a recognizable block rather than an isolated cipher. It also participates in the wider muqaṭṭaʿāt pattern where raw letters are followed by Book or revelation language: 46:2 answers the letter-threshold with the descent of the Book, as comparable openings do at 2:1-2 and 3:1-3. Sonically, the movement from pharyngeal {{ar:ح}} ({{tr:ḥāʾ}}) to bilabial {{ar:م}} ({{tr:mīm}}) makes the speech apparatus itself audible before propositional speech unfolds. The main payoff is convergence: grammar withholds clause roles, rootlessness blocks false derivation, script compresses two recited units, pause and madd shape the hearing, controlled classical readings thicken the sign-value, cluster recurrence locates it, and 46:2 turns the threshold toward revealed discourse.

topics.headline: outside sentence grammar
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah is complete before any governor, case role, predicate, or ordinary clause relation begins.
topics.reason: The QAC row explicitly treats the item as disconnected letters with no iʿrāb or syntactic role, and translation support warns against expanding it into ordinary lexical words.

topics.headline: opacity works as threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that unresolved sign-value is not a gap to fill but part of how the opener marks the threshold before discourse.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows coherently describe the muqaṭṭaʿa surface as meaningful undecidability and semantic density, while guardrail evidence keeps it from becoming an ordinary paraphrased lexical item.

topics.headline: named letters and sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps both sides active: the opener is recited as named letters and also arrives as elemental sound before words begin.
topics.reason: The local surface is a disconnected-letter item; the CRITICAL rows preserve its dual status as letter-name object and performed phonetic material without contradicting the non-lexical parse.

topics.headline: rootless form blocks derivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader knows not to search for a triliteral root meaning behind the opener; its analyzable material is the letter-pair as written and recited.
topics.reason: The aligned QAC word has no root or form tag, and there are no V4 local root branches to activate; this supports rootless analysis without treating missing dictionary evidence as semantic absence.

topics.headline: concealed divine-name pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel a concealed mercy-name pressure from {{ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰن}} ({{tr:al-Raḥmān}}) while the visible opener remains disconnected letters rather than a spelled-out name.
topics.reason: The abbreviation theory survives as a classical secondary reading, but QAC and translation evidence keep the local surface from being translated as the divine name itself.

topics.headline: decree formula as secondary pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register the ḥumma al-amr possibility, with its sense of the matter having been decreed, while still hearing the local word as the same rootless letter-pair.
topics.reason: The alternative reading may thicken the sign-value, but it must be narrowed because the canonical local parse is disconnected letters with no ordinary predication or lexical expansion.

topics.headline: one written token, two recited units
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the formal tension: one visible word-row binds two named letters, while madd and recitation make the compact writing expand in sound.
topics.reason: The alignment gives one word for the whole ayah, and the CRITICAL rows press the fused script and recitational marking as a local formal payoff.

topics.headline: pause exposes two beats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the ayah as two stopped letter beats while preserving the same written pair and non-lexical status.
topics.reason: The waqf evidence survives as acoustic pacing and boundary texture, but it does not create two lexical words, change the consonantal inventory, or add a syntactic parse.

topics.headline: oath pressure without qasam form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel oath-like solemnity from the isolated letters without mistaking the opener for a formal oath construction.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row's oath-pressure survives, but it must be narrowed because the surface lacks the ordinary qasam particles and case-marked sworn object.

topics.headline: final node in the seven-surah series
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes 46:1 as the closing member of the contiguous {{ar:حمٓ}} ({{tr:ḥā mīm}}) opener series at 40:1, 41:1, 42:1, 43:1, 44:1, 45:1, and 46:1.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL evidence gives concrete recurrence across 40:1 through 46:1; no guardrail evidence contradicts treating the local ayah as part of that recognizable macro-unit.

topics.headline: letters before the Book statement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sequence from raw letters in 46:1 to the explicit Book-descent wording in 46:2, a local instance of the wider muqaṭṭaʿāt-and-revelation pattern also seen at 2:1-2 and 3:1-3.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give a concrete local continuation into 46:2 and named comparanda at 2:1-2 and 3:1-3; this supports directional uptake without inventing a new local lexical sense.

topics.headline: one beat before assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entire ayah is a sealed pre-propositional threshold, so the next verse arrives as payload after the opener rather than as syntax inside it.
topics.reason: The input has one QAC word, no clause attachments, and no internal verbal or nominal frame, so the structural payoff is whole-ayah threshold placement.

topics.headline: throat-to-lips articulation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a bodily arc of speech: the opener starts deep in the throat and resolves at the lips before ordinary discourse begins.
topics.reason: Because the local word is rootless and non-clausal, the phonetic observation survives as sound-shape payoff without becoming a lexical root claim.

topics.headline: mechanisms converge at the threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why a two-letter ayah can carry so much force: grammar, form, sound, polyvalence, recurrence, and forward uptake all point to language before lexical statement.
topics.reason: The synthesis row gathers the surviving grammatical, formal, phonetic, semantic, structural, and inter-ayah payoffs rather than adding an unrelated claim.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The entire ayah is the isolated two-letter utterance حم, with no rooted morpheme or ordinary clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: Naming the two letters forces a pause at the surah boundary: the reader first encounters sound and sequence without a lexical proposition. The underdetermination creates attention before semantic expansion.

changed_reading.before: A bare pair of disconnected letters with no recoverable lexical claim.
changed_reading.after: An attention-setting oral threshold whose first action is to make the pair be heard in sequence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Two ordinary Arabic letters are detached from words and placed as a complete ayah.
baseline_models.mechanism: Detachment exposes letters as compositional material. A minimal pair can therefore be carried as a compact kernel rather than decoded as a word.

changed_reading.before: An opaque token awaiting a hidden lexical expansion.
changed_reading.after: A display of minimal alphabetic material, complete at two units yet available for later composition.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The pair is syntactically unattached and semantically unfilled while still bounded as a complete ayah.
baseline_models.mechanism: Because it is both complete and unresolved, it can function as a signature-like boundary that withholds referential content and makes the reader's interpretive stance unusually visible.

changed_reading.before: An accidental or purely decorative heading.
changed_reading.after: A deliberately bounded opaque sign whose refusal to paraphrase is part of its effect.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate sequence couples downward arrival with the ordering of letters into a written Book. The isolated pair now reads as the compressed ingress of a discourse that expands one ayah later into composed scripture.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies caused descent and arrival, turning the static opening into an ingress vector.
The branch supplies letters ordered as writing, making the pair the minimal material from which the Book expands.

structural_cues: 46:1 is a complete rootless ayah immediately followed, without an intervening proposition, by the nominal identification of the Book's descent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate adjacency, descent, and ordered writing; I infer a compression-to-expansion arrow from the pair into the Book. A live alternative is that حم only marks a boundary before an independent declaration.

changed_reading.before: A generic display of two detached alphabetic units.
changed_reading.after: A compact threshold of descent: minimal letters poised to unfold as the composed Book.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah demands a prior Book or residual mark of knowledge, then identifies this discourse as composed writing in an Arabic linguistic medium. Since حم exposes that medium before any word, the pair can act as material evidence rather than a hidden lexical message.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies a surviving mark that points beyond itself, giving the bare letters an evidentiary rather than lexical role.
The branch supplies ordered letters as written text, linking the isolated units to both books named in the ayah.
The branch supplies language as spoken expression, relocating the pair inside a shared linguistic medium.
The branch supplies clear articulation, allowing raw letter-material to anticipate the discourse's later explicitness.

structural_cues: The opening is nonlexical but visibly consists of Arabic letters; 46:4 frames proof through a book or trace of knowledge, and 46:12 names an Arabic tongue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a demand for textual evidence and an Arabic linguistic vehicle; I infer that the bare pair exhibits the shared material of that vehicle before it asserts anything. It may instead be a conventional marker with no argumentative work.

changed_reading.before: An opaque pair presumed to conceal a separate meaning.
changed_reading.after: The threshold displays its medium: shared Arabic letter-material appears before the Book argues in articulated Arabic.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later recitation is explicitly sequential sound; mere possession of hearing fails, while attentive listeners fall silent and report having heard. This recasts the letter names as an initial listening event that sorts auditory contact from receptive uptake.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies one voice following another, highlighting the opening as an ordered acoustic sequence.
The branch extends hearing into understanding and compliance; its failure here separates acoustic capacity from uptake.
The branch supplies direct perception of sound, grounding the contrasting listeners in an actual auditory event.
The branch supplies attentive silence, making receptivity rather than instant decoding the operative response.

structural_cues: 46:26 lists hearing among faculties that did not avail deniers; 46:29-30 stages the opposite sequence of listening, silence, completion, and a report of hearing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies recited sequence and a contrast between failed hearing and attentive silence; I infer that the sounded opening begins this response test. The alternative is that the contrast concerns the Qur'an generally and does not specialize حم.

changed_reading.before: An oral threshold that merely arrests attention.
changed_reading.after: A diagnostic first sound: حم asks whether the hearer merely receives phonemes or enters attentive, responsive hearing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context repeatedly opposes what a sign discloses to the category imposed on it: clear recitation is called deception or falsehood, and a presented cloud is seen as welcome rain before being identified as destructive wind. Applied to the maximally underdetermined opening, opacity becomes a controlled test of projection.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies meaning disclosed through speech or sign, establishing the context's claim that the presentation is legible.
The branch supplies deceptive redirection, functioning as the audience's imposed category for the disclosed sign.
The branch supplies inversion away from a proper direction, sharpening misreading as an active turn rather than missing data.
The branch supplies visual and inward seeing, locating the mistaken classification in the perceiver's act.
The branch supplies something newly appearing from a direction, a low-information presentation awaiting a reading.
The branch supplies rain descending from cloud, the hopeful interpretation projected onto the appearance.
The branch supplies moving air or wind, the materially different reality that reverses the projected rain reading.

structural_cues: 46:7 and 46:11 record hostile renaming of the discourse; 46:24 narrates one visible presentation whose audience-assigned reading is immediately reversed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated misclassification and one explicit appearance-to-rain-to-wind reversal; I infer that the opening's lack of a lexeme can expose the same receiver-side projection. Its opacity may instead have no deliberate diagnostic function.

changed_reading.before: An opaque sign that merely blocks understanding.
changed_reading.after: A low-information sign that makes the reader's interpretive reflex visible before the surah supplies its own categories.

context_deltas.mechanism: A heard discourse sends listeners toward their people, where hearing becomes call and demanded response; the closing delivery term frames completed transmission. The opening pair can therefore be carried as a compact relay signal, not only privately decoded.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies receipt of sound, the first transfer point in the relay.
The branch supplies turning the face toward a destination, converting reception into directed return to a community.
The branch supplies a vocal call that draws another, making onward transmission explicitly social.
The branch supplies a returned answer, defining the relay's intended completion as response rather than repetition alone.
The branch supplies delivery of a message, allowing the surah's closing notice to complete the opening signal's transmission arc.

structural_cues: 46:29-31 forms a hear-turn-call-answer sequence, while 46:35 closes the surah with a one-word delivery notice.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a transmission chain from hearing through communal response to final delivery; I infer that حم can serve as its minimal initial token. The live alternative is that this relay belongs to the Qur'an as a whole and only secondarily colors the opening pair.

changed_reading.before: A private threshold encountered by an individual reader or hearer.
changed_reading.after: A minimal transmissible cue whose proper completion is communal relay and response.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a rootless pair through the consonantal echo ح-م in ح م ل and through deliberately branch-distant pregnancy images, not through morphology. It remains anchored in the exact ordered letter pair and gains a coherent carry-gather-release sequence from 46:15 and 46:29. Downstream prose should render it only as a latent formal analogy, never as an etymology or asserted decoding of حم.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The ordered letters ح then م form the entire opening and recur, still in order, at the head of the contextual root ح م ل.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies an inwardly carried pregnancy or fruit, turning the shared consonant frame into latent content held before emergence.
The branch supplies the mother as bearer and nurturer, locating the carrying mechanism in the ayah's explicit maternal sequence.
The branch supplies delivery and release of a carried load, giving the latent kernel an outward transition.
The branch supplies separation of child from mother or nursing, completing emergence as differentiation rather than mere exposure.
The branch supplies a womb gathering a pregnancy, creating the branch-distant bridge from carried kernel to the recited Qur'an.

changed_reading.before: The letters are an arbitrary sealed pair with no internal motion.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, ح-م is a gestational consonantal kernel: content is carried and gathered, then separated into articulated recitation.

strongest_changes: The immediate descent and writing branches of 46:2 change the pair from generic letter-material into a compressed entrance for the composed Book.
The failed-hearing versus attentive-listening sequence of 46:26 and 46:29-30 changes the sounded pair into a diagnostic response threshold.
The repeated renaming and the cloud-to-rain-to-wind reversal change opacity from mere blockage into a possible test of reader projection.
The hear-turn-call-answer-deliver chain changes a private opening token into a socially relayed signal.
summary.what_was_special: A rootless two-letter ayah could support no focus branch citation of its own. Its formal underdetermination therefore remained the anchor while context activated compositional, acoustic, evidentiary, diagnostic, social, and gestational mechanisms without forcing one decoding.
remaining_uncertainties: The compression-to-Book relation may be functional, or it may arise only from immediate adjacency.
The projection test may characterize reception of the discourse generally rather than the opening pair specifically.
The relay model is strongest for the recited Book as a whole and only inferentially begins with حم.
The gestational ح-م echo is formal and branch-distant, not a lexical derivation.

channel_generated_outputs.usage: External source manifest only. These generated outputs may inform channel-family/path context when the agent has file access, but first-pass review limits still apply: no established channel name, accept/reject claim, or maturity claim unless a future adjudicated ledger is present.

unresolved.reason: no compatible span in the best ordered source alignment

morphemes_tsv.note: ayah attribution taken from qac_ref, with non-surah rows and standalone basmala ayah marker rows (1:0) filtered out | dropped_preface_rows=7

word_morpheme_spans.note: Ordered surface alignment within canonical QAC words; only spans shared by all best alignments are joined. Upstream word-analysis identities and wording are preserved. Unresolved analytic units remain available for qualified reading; never infer their QAC identity from upstream numbering.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref resolves against qac_morphemes for this ayah

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. This ayah has QAC morpheme rows but no lexical roots, so the surah-scope branch inventory has no ayah root to retain. The empty scoped inventory is deliberate for rootless units such as muqatta'at, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

butuncul_okuma.note: no whole-surah reading file exists for this surah

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
